# İstekler Meydanı 2.0 — Dilekler Festivali
**3 November 2026 · First region of Cümle Meydanı · Mission 5 of 6**

## Educational intent
A child must communicate a preference, polite request, negative preference, or an articulated reason in English. There is no price, currency arithmetic, shop simulation, LLM free text, or unmoderated communication: this is an English language learning game.

**Grammar is editorially authored**, never generated by unconstrained grammar substitution. Turkish semantic cues match the child's requested English meaning, and the visual response must match affirmative versus negative preference. Independent production is distinguished from prompted/assisted solutions.

## Four real festival chapters
| Chapter | English learning | Real game interaction |
|--|--|--|
| **Lezzetler Bahçesi** | I like / I do not like / because | Choose a food from an eight-illustration market, choose affirmative/negative intent, assemble the whole sentence; negative preferences visibly reject fruit |
| **Nezaket Tezgâhı** | I want ... please / Can I have some ... please? / Could I have some ... please? | Identify correct item, choose English politeness word, place polite order and serve the guest |
| **Karakter Sohbeti** | Like versus want versus dislike, affirmative/negative dialogue, "would like" | Read or listen to festival guest's request, choose communicative intent, give meaningful English answer |
| **Büyük Festival Sofrası** | and (two likes), but (want versus don't want), because + adjectives, prefer ... to ... | Choose primary/secondary item(s) and (A2) reason, express combined meaning, visibly change festival serving |

Four original illustrated guests: Mila, Leo, Luna, Niko. Eight original illustrated foods: apples, bananas, oranges, grapes, carrots, strawberries, pears, peaches. Each session varies selected character/food/phrases and prioritizes past weakness and previously learned foods.

## Two strictly independent difficulty axes
| Profile grade | Tasks per chapter | Total | Max sentence tokens | Estimated playtime |
|--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Grades 1–2 | 3 | 12 | 10 | 8–12 minutes |
| Grades 3–4 / unselected | 4 | 16 | 13 for grades 3–4, 19 if unselected | 11–16 minutes |
| Grades 5–8 | 5 | 20 | 19 | 14–19 minutes |

- **Pre-A1:** very short affirmative preference and polite request; simple `and` combination in final. No forced A1/A2 grammar because the pupil's school grade is high.
- **A1:** `do not like`, `Can I have ... please?`, `I would like ...`, `but` in preference contrast, formal readable questions.
- **A2:** `because they are sweet/juicy/crunchy`, `Could I have ... please?`, `I prefer X to Y because ...`, with shortened context for young pupils. Placement remains stored profile's original level, never auto-promoted from grade.
- All tasks are within exact word limits, contain a meaningful Turkish cue and reflect illustrated objects. No gameplay time-out, speed punishment, or randomly corrupted English grammar.

## Visual and audio implementation
- Original responsive illustration: a 1200×660 layered SVG festival city, tent awnings, city tower, bunting, fairytale backgrounds, magical lighting and animated particles; four original SVG portrait characters and eight individually authored vector fruits.
- Uses existing `story_castle.webp` **only** as hero background art where appropriate. SVG is used for all characters and ingredients that must respond to play, avoiding blurry raster stretching.
- Chosen food enters the festival serving basket. Secondary object shows wanted/not wanted meaning. Negative preferences are crossed visually. Success triggers customer celebration, English pronunciation and automatic progression.
- Responsive desktop/touch layouts, focus-visible controls, aria-labels and reduced-motion mode. Global sound opt-in/mute/ducking and dedicated original `wishes` procedural music scene. Recorded native human speech is not claimed.

## Persistence and integrity
- Existing profile, game ID **`island_sentence_square_plaza`**, level ID **5**, and `saveSentencePlazaMission` remain canonical. Missions 1–4/6 and their stars unaffected.
- 12/16/20 answers are written atomically to existing progress events at full mission completion; no partial earned stars. Unique session ID means retry-safe idempotency.
- Every answer records a stable task ID, first-try success, mistakes, hint/audio assistance, communicative kind and time. Result score is educational evidence, not certification.
- Versioned **same-device** localStorage checkpoint stores unfinished session, its selected English placement & grade, position and evidence; incompatible/stale checkpoint discarded. Full progress remains in existing repository/sync infrastructure. **Cross-device mid-session resume is not implemented.**
- Same profile's Word Garden food recall history can prioritize familiar vocabulary.
- No new SQL, no Vercel deploy, no app store publishing.

## Acceptance gates
Automated:
- [ ] TypeScript compilation
- [ ] Full web regression, profile isolation, session idempotence, grade×placement curriculum tests
- [ ] Next.js production build and static Android web export
- [ ] Android debug APK and iOS simulator compilation when CI supports them

Human checks still needed:
- [ ] Product owner local play of all four stages
- [ ] Grade 1 Pre-A1 and grade 8 Pre-A1 on real phone, no CEFR leakage
- [ ] A1/A2 English teacher checks all English+Turkish cues and festival scene semantics
- [ ] Mute/low-volume/TTS intelligibility, browser without speechSynthesis, reduced motion
- [ ] Exit mid-chapter, reopen same profile on same device, resume without double rewards
- [ ] Two-device sync and offline/reconnect tests
- [ ] Real children comprehension, motor access and play-time research

**Scope honesty:** This is the first playable Cümle Meydanı region mission #5, not the next four locked regions. The "premium" art and gameplay are programmed, but teacher and child-device QA remain acceptance prerequisites.
